How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were a number of different accommodations. Most exchange students, including myself, stayed at either Walter Gage or Fairview Crescent.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were cooking facilities available in the unit. One of the accommodations had a canteen (which was also available for a fee).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Most of the people you'll stay with are a bit younger, and you are likely to experience a different approach to regular cleaning, as it seems a lot of them are living away from their parents for the first time.

However, the accommodation is quite a bit cheaper in most cases than if you had to find housing in other parts of Vancouver.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
In the spring/summer prior to going you had to send in a list of 10 courses in a specific priority. However, this is not as important as you'll receive a more formal registration process link, where you'll have to register for courses on a first-come-first-served basis.

It is important to know that you'll be able to opt-out of the courses and opt-in to other courses within the first two weeks or so upon the start of the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: All the help needed in an academic context was provided in a orientation meeting held in the first week at the faculty.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: For the most part I felt as though I got the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As it is first-come-first-served obviously registering early (sometime in the summer prior to my exchange) is helpful. Also - for law students atleast - an exam schedule was available (meaning something like 9-10 prior to the exams) at the same as registering for courses. It would be helpful to scoop this out through the Peter A. Allard Law website.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Apply for grants (legater) early and make sure you apply for a lot.

Connect with other UCPH, DTU, CBS (etc.) students before you go.

Make sure you do social activities.
